text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Hosni Mubarak discusses with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat the latest developments in negotiations with Israel. Arafat says the negotiations are currently "paralysed".
- An earthquake measuring 4.5 on the open-ended Richter scale shook the the southern area of the Gulf of Suez on Friday morning.

- Greek President Costis Stephanopoulos says at arrival in Cairo on Friday that his talks with Mubarak will deal with bilateral issues and the Middle East. Stephanopoulos will stay three days in Egypt.
- A joint committee from the tourist promotion agency and the Red Sea province will discuss 66 new tourist projects in the province next week.
- Economic Affairs Minister Youssef Boutros Ghali says:"Our economy has surpassed the crisis stage."He says the Egyptian economy has turned into a "future-building economy".
- The interior ministry is planning to sell off its headquarters in the heart of the capital, assistant minister Major General Raouf el-Mennawi says. The ministry will move to the suburb of Abbasiya.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri will deliver the government's statement at the Parliament on Monday morning.
- Youssef Boutros Ghali says Egypt is seeking to achieve a growth rate of seven percent by the end of the century.
- Thirty three hand guns disappeared from civil defence depots.
